exposure: Gestational age at exposure to antimicrobial agents
Type of antimicrobial used (first-generation cephalosporins vs. third-generation cephalosporins)
First-generation cephalosporins use vs. no antimicrobial use
First-generation cephalosporins use vs. third-generation cephalosporins use
outcome: Admission of neonate to the NICU
cohort: 370 pregnant patients in 22 tertiary hospitals in China
finding: The study found that both first- and third-generation cephalosporins use during pregnancy was associated with an increased risk of adverse pregnancy and neonatal outcomes, with first-generation cephalosporins posing a higher risk compared to third-generation cephalosporins.
mod_finding: The study controlled for cesarean section but did not investigate any associations between mode of delivery and antimicrobial use.
gest_age: Mentioned as a confounding factor, but no specific values provided
